title: Book Three · Chapter 141: The Next Name
story:
The following Wednesday, the teacher asks Ronan about a music afternoon.

It is a small school event on Friday, from three until four. A few students will sing or play. The teacher needs someone to introduce them.

“Would you like that part?”

Ronan looks at the short list.

“Yes.”

The teacher gives him the names and song titles. He needs to check the order with the performers before Friday.

After lunch, he finds one girl with a guitar. She is practising in an empty classroom.

Ronan waits at the door until she stops.

“Can I check your part?”

She puts the guitar across her knees and looks at the list.

Her name and title are right. She wants a chair near the front.

“Do you want the chair there first?” he asks.

“Yes. Then I can sit down with this.”

She touches the guitar.

Ronan writes chair beside her name.

He tries the introduction quietly from his list.

The girl corrects one sound in her name. Ronan says it again and checks her face.

“Yes. Like that.”

He puts a little mark beside the name. Then he tries the whole introduction once more.

The girl lifts the guitar from her knees. Ronan begins to speak again, but she is still finding a comfortable place for the strap.

“Not yet,” she says, smiling.

He stops. She moves the guitar, sits straight, then rests both feet on the floor.

“Now?”

“Yes.”

This time, he waits until she looks toward him before he says the words.

The empty classroom has only a few chairs in front of them. On Friday, there will be people in those places. Ronan wants the beginning to sound smooth.

The girl tries a few notes. He keeps his pencil still until she finishes.

She looks down at his page again. He has written the right name and title. Now she points to the space beside the note about the chair.

“Say my name when I'm ready,” she adds. “I will look up.”

“All right.”

He checks the next two performers. One is singing with a friend. The other needs space beside the window.

By the end, his clean list has notes along both sides.

He takes the list back to the teacher. She checks the spaces and agrees to put the chair near the front before three.

Kai looks at it on Thursday.

“You have a lot to say.”

“Mostly names.”

“Say mine.”

Ronan stands beside his desk.

“And now, Kai.”

Kai lifts both hands. “Thank you. That is the whole song.”

Anna laughs from the next desk. Ronan sits down and puts the list away before the lesson starts.

At lunch, he asks if she can come on Friday.

“After my drawing talk,” she says. “The teacher has time at three. I may miss the first part.”

He looks at the first name on his list.

“I will look for you later.”

She nods. “Tell me about the beginning afterward.”

After school, Ronan tries the opening words in the empty classroom. The rows of chairs seem very long from the front.

He speaks once, then starts again more slowly.

The girl with the guitar passes the door. She stops to listen to the last line.

“I can hear you,” she says.

“The chairs look doubtful.”

She smiles. “They are a quiet audience.”

Ronan laughs and lowers the page. She carries the guitar away, and he checks the Friday time once more before he goes home.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

introduce＝介绍上场；performer＝表演者；title＝曲名、标题；audience＝观众。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan承担的是哪一段工作？他实际向表演者问清了什么需要？
2. Anna为什么可能错过开头？Ronan怎样回应？

## 读句子

**By the end, his clean list has notes along both sides.**

拆开看：By the end, / his clean list / has notes / along both sides.

到核对完时／原本干净的名单／写了备注／两侧都有。
